def: The plan and process side of quality: procedures, plans and audits that give confidence the work will meet requirements.
quote: quality assurance versus quality control

def: Checking the actual work: inspecting and testing what was installed against the requirements.
quote: quality assurance versus quality control

def: The list of inspections and tests for each work step, who does them, the acceptance criteria and the hold and witness points.
quote: Acceptance criteria Measurable limits a test result must meet.

def: A point in the ITP where work stops until the named party has inspected and signed off.
A point in the ITP where a party is invited to watch a test or inspection; work may go on if they do not attend.
quote: witnessed by the owner's commissioning team

def: Product data, shop drawings or samples sent for approval before the material is bought and installed.
quote: ensure compliance with contract documents

def: A written question to the designer when drawings or specs are unclear or conflict; never guess.
quote: RFIs (Requests for Information)

def: The record of work or material that does not meet requirements, from identification and containment through disposition, fix, re-inspection and closure.
quote: The issues log, with every item closed or formally accepted with a plan.

def: Corrective action fixes the problem found and its cause; preventive action stops it happening elsewhere or again.
The list of small remaining defects and incomplete items to fix before handover.
Drawings red-lined to show what was really installed, so they match the finished facility.
quote: As-built drawings and single-line diagrams that match the installed facility

def: Proving equipment and systems work as designed, level by level from factory tests to integrated systems testing (L1 to L5).
quote: Commissioning a data center involves thousands of individual tests

def: Checking delivered material against the order and approved submittal, and for shipping damage, before it is accepted or installed.
quote: Receiving inspection, pre-functional checklists, torque checks, labeling

def: Making sure only the current, controlled revision of each drawing and procedure is used in the field.
quote: is by definition uncontrolled and may be out of date

def: The documentation handed to operations for a system: test records, issues log, as-builts, settings, manuals and training.
quote: Turnover package The documentation handed to operations for a system.

def: The system that watches a fab's cleanroom air, chilled and process water, ultrapure water, gases, power and alarms.
quote: Chiller plant and PCW, ultrapure water, bulk and specialty gases, vacuum and abatement in one facility overview.

def: Checking each field device through to the controller and the displayed value or alarm, typically at commissioning Level 3.
quote: the commissioning team verifies controls point by point

def: The fixed part of a copper channel, for example patch panel to outlet; at most 90 m. It is what gets certified.
quote: The maximum permitted length of the permanent link is 90 meters.

def: The whole path from one active device to another including patch and equipment cords; at most 100 m.
quote: the channel is the connection from one active device to another

def: How much signal is lost along a cable or link, in dB; measured on copper certification and fiber Tier 1 tests.
quote: Insertion Loss (IL)

def: Signal leaking from one pair into another at the same end; excess untwisting at terminations is a common cause of NEXT failures.
quote: excessive untwisting is a leading cause of NEXT failures

def: Signal reflected back toward the source by impedance changes in the link.
quote: Return Loss (RL)

def: The certification test that checks each conductor lands on the right pin at both ends (opens, shorts, crossed or split pairs).
The tightest a cable may be bent: UTP 4 x OD, shielded 8 x OD, fiber 20 x OD while pulling and 10 x installed.
quote: UTP should not be bent tighter than four times the cable's outer diameter

def: A tested and listed system that restores a fire-rated wall or floor where cables pass through it; inspected before it is covered.
quote: Firestop systems must not be concealed from view before being inspected and approved

def: The area a camera actually sees; together with pixel density it decides what the camera can be used for.
quote: the pixel density and the field of view

def: Single-mode (OS2) has a tiny core for long runs; multimode (OM3/OM4/OM5) has a larger core for shorter runs.
quote: singlemode or multimode

def: The expected loss of a fiber link: connectors + splices + length x attenuation, compared with the measured loss.
quote: is calculated using typical component losses for each part of the cable plant

def: The meter that, with a matched light source, measures fiber link loss in Tier 1 testing.
quote: Optical power meter (#2) calibrated at the same wavelengths as the source output.

def: The Tier 2 instrument that draws a trace of a fiber, showing splices, connectors, faults and length.
quote: It can verify splice loss, measure length and find faults.

def: Joining two fibers by melting them together; about 0.15 dB on single-mode, 0.3 dB maximum.
quote: 0.15dB for singlemode fusion splices

def: A short cord with connectors used to connect equipment or cross-connect; part of the channel, not the permanent link.
quote: standards recommend 5 meter patch cords

def: Making sure the transmitter at one end reaches the receiver at the other.
quote: Transition methods used to maintain optical fiber polarity

def: The polished tip of a fiber connector, inspected and graded by zone under IEC 61300-3-35.
quote: Zone A (core), Zone B (cladding), Zone C (adhesive), and Zone D (contact/ferrule)

def: The pulling force on a cable during installation; never above the lowest of the conductor, device and manufacturer limits.
quote: maximum pulling tensions

def: The crushing force on a cable as it is pulled around a bend; often the most restrictive limit.
quote: Sidewall Pressure (SP) is exerted on a cable as it is pulled around a bend.

def: A support system for cables, not a raceway (NEC Article 392).
quote: A cable tray is a support system for cables.

def: The current a conductor can carry continuously without exceeding its temperature rating.
quote: Ampacity in Cable Tray Works Differently

def: A DC test of how well cable insulation resists leakage, in megohms; done de-energized and locked out.
quote: Insulation resistance should be approximately one megohm for each 1,000 volts of operating voltage

def: Isolating energy sources and applying your own lock and tag so equipment cannot be energized while people work on it.
quote: Lockout devices and tagout devices shall be singularly identified

def: The explosive release of heat and light from an electrical fault; the arc flash boundary is where incident energy reaches 1.2 cal/cm2.
quote: if an electrical arc flash were to occur

def: Connecting a conductor or fiber to its lug, terminal, jack or connector.
quote: increased resistance over time at the termination

def: The tightening force on a bolted or screw terminal; applied with a calibrated tool to the manufacturer's value and recorded.
quote: requires the use of a torque tool to terminate conductors

def: Marking each power conductor's phase at both ends and at every pull box so terminations land correctly.
Checking each conductor is unbroken end to end, and not shorted to others or to ground.
quote: Tests for conductor continuity can include a simple check with an ohmmeter
